title: Which Fruits Are Highest in Potassium?

seo.title: Which Fruits Are Highest in Potassium?
seo.meta_description: Bananas are a good source of potassium, but they are not the highest. Compare avocado, guava, banana, kiwi, and dried fruit by 100 grams and serving.
seo.search_intent: Identify fruits that provide the most potassium and compare real amounts.

excerpt: Bananas are a useful potassium source, but they do not top the list. Per 100 grams, avocado provides about 485 mg, guava about 417 mg, and banana about 358 mg; dried fruit can be much more concentrated because much of its water has been removed.
content_html:
Bananas and potassium are almost synonymous in everyday nutrition advice, but the shorthand hides a more interesting ranking. Several fruits match or exceed bananas per 100 grams, and dried fruit can contain much more because water has been removed.

A practical fresh-fruit comparison

Typical USDA FoodData Central values per 100 grams are roughly: avocado 485 mg, guava 417 mg, banana 358 mg, kiwi about 310 mg, and cantaloupe about 267 mg.

For context, an apple is around 107 mg per 100 grams and an orange around 180 mg. That means 100 grams of avocado can provide roughly four and a half times as much potassium as the same weight of apple.

Dried fruit is far more concentrated

The NIH lists 755 mg of potassium in 1/2 cup of dried apricots, 635 mg in 1/2 cup of prunes, and 618 mg in 1/2 cup of raisins. Removing water concentrates minerals—but also concentrates calories and sugars per bite.

So “highest potassium” does not automatically mean “best choice in unlimited amounts.” Serving size matters.

Serving size can change the ranking

A medium banana provides about 422 mg of potassium. A half cup of cantaloupe has about 214 mg, while a cup of orange juice can provide about 496 mg. Comparing foods only by 100 grams is useful scientifically, but not always how people actually eat them.

Fruit is only one source

Potatoes, beans and lentils, vegetables, dairy foods, nuts, fish, and meat also contribute meaningful potassium. NIH recommends meeting potassium needs through a varied diet rather than chasing one “superfood.” Current U.S. adequate intakes are 3,400 mg per day for adult men and 2,600 mg for adult women.

More potassium is not always appropriate

People with chronic kidney disease or those taking certain medications may need to limit potassium. In that situation, a “high-potassium fruit” ranking should not be treated as a recommendation to eat more without individualized medical advice.

For healthy adults trying to diversify potassium sources, avocado, guava, banana, kiwi, cantaloupe, and modest portions of dried fruit are all useful options.

faq.question: Are bananas the fruit highest in potassium?
faq.answer: No. They are a good source, but avocado and guava can provide more per 100 grams, while dried fruits are much more concentrated.

faq.question: How much potassium is in a medium banana?
faq.answer: About 422 mg according to the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements.

faq.question: Can everyone eat lots of high-potassium fruit?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. People with kidney disease or certain medications may need to control potassium intake.
